review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–101). It defines three things: `unitBitStep`, `flatUnitWalk` and `unitJointDraw`. `unitBitStep` is `Option.getD` applied to `smallBitProposal`. `flatUnitWalk` is the project's `wordWalk` composed with `GridBoundary.gridWordEquiv`. `unitJointDraw` pairs the walk output `z` with `fallback z` in the sigma type `PaperStateJoint`. All three use existing operations and are named specialisations of this development's Boolean-sampling pipeline. The rubric says that implementing a named API through a generic map or composition does not make it redundant.

The probability machinery the file relies on is `RationalLaw` (ℚ-valued finite laws), with `mapLaw`, `uniformLaw`, `pointLaw`, `variation`, `walkLaw` and `dependentJointLaw`. It is defined in other files: `ResidualMixture.lean`, `FirstSuccess.lean`, `RationalWalks.lean` and `FiniteDependentLaw.lean`. It does not compete with Mathlib's `PMF` or `Measure` within this file, so I made no claim against it. The ℚ-valued representation looks deliberate: the docstring says "exactly represented rational masses", and the proofs mix ℚ and ℝ casts through `Rat.cast_le`. Any consolidation question belongs to the files that define `RationalLaw`, not to this one.

Sibling files have parallel step and draw definitions: `unitCodeBitStep` and `unitCodeJointDraw` in `UnitProfileSemantics.lean` and `UnitFiniteLaw.lean`, and `smallJointDraw` in `FirstPaperBooleanDraw.lean`. They use different proposal maps, so they are not the same concept as the ones here. They are also not Mathlib concepts, so I did not report them. There was no clear Mathlib counterpart for any definition in this file, so I abstain. I did not read the `FirstSuccess.lean` definitions beyond the first 180 lines or the remaining `RationalLaw` copies in other namespaces, because they lie outside the target file.
